properties.natural_language: The Altair fork upgrade must execute at a deterministic slot such that all clients transition state identically; the resulting Altair state must be a pure function of the Phase 0 pre-state.
Before upgrade_to_altair executes, the current slot must equal the configured ALTAIR_FORK_EPOCH * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH, and the beacon state must be a valid Phase 0 state.

After translate_participation completes, every pending attestation from Phase 0 must have its participation flags correctly set in the new Altair participation arrays, with no attestation lost or duplicated.

The sync committee assigned during fork upgrade must contain exactly SYNC_COMMITTEE_SIZE validators, and duplicating it to current and next sync committee must not reduce the effective committee diversity.
After the fork field update, state.fork.previous_version equals the Phase 0 fork version, state.fork.current_version equals the Altair fork version, and state.fork.epoch equals ALTAIR_FORK_EPOCH.
After participation flag translation, every valid pending attestation must have exactly the correct source, target, and head flags set based on its inclusion delay and data.
After inactivity score initialization, all validators must have their inactivity scores set to zero in the new Altair state.
After sync committee computation, current_sync_committee and next_sync_committee must both be set and equal, each containing SYNC_COMMITTEE_SIZE member public keys.
Genesis configuration fetched from the genesis server must be validated for integrity (e.g., hash verification) before the node uses it for chain initialization.
The bootnode peer list received from the Ethereum Foundation bootnode must contain valid ENR records with proper signatures before connection attempts.
No production-value transactions or assets must exist on the ephemeral testnet; the testnet must be treated as disposable with no security guarantees for stored value.
The testnet destruction schedule must be clearly defined and communicated; all nodes must shut down gracefully when the testnet lifecycle ends.
The consensus mechanism for the ephemeral testnet must be explicitly specified in the genesis configuration before any block production begins.
Contract bytecode submitted by developers must be validated for EIP-specific opcode support before deployment on the testnet.
After executing an experimental opcode, the execution result state must accurately reflect success or failure with appropriate error codes.

All signing requests from the beacon node must be checked against the persistent slashing protection database before any signature is produced. Block proposals must not sign for a slot already signed. Attestations must not create double or surround votes.
Attestation target epoch must not be more than ~6 hours (ATTESTATION_SAFETY_DECAY epochs) in the future relative to the validator's local clock.
Committee assignments received from the beacon node must be used for attestation duty only at the correct slot and committee index; the validator must verify assignment validity.
The slashing protection database must persist across validator client restarts. Loss of this database must prevent all signing operations until manually resolved.
The validator's local clock must be synchronized with the network within acceptable bounds for correct slot and epoch timing of attestation and proposal duties.
When a beacon node returns an invalid block for signing, the validator client must reject it; the specific rejection behavior and error reporting must be well-defined.
A validator that has both a pending voluntary exit and a pending slashing must have the slashing take precedence; the exit must not cancel or override the slashing penalty.
After attestation creation, the attestation data must reference the correct source checkpoint, target checkpoint, and beacon block root for the assigned slot.
After aggregator selection check, if the validator is selected as aggregator, it must collect attestations for the correct committee and produce a valid aggregate with selection proof.
After block construction, the signed block must contain a valid RANDAO reveal, a correct ETH1 vote, and all included operations must be valid and within limits.
All attestations received from P2P gossip must be fully validated for signature correctness, committee membership, and slot timing before being accepted.
Aggregate-and-proof messages received from P2P must verify the selection proof, aggregator index validity, and the aggregate BLS signature before acceptance.
ETH1 deposit data must include valid Merkle proofs. ETH1 block vote candidates must satisfy the follow distance requirement and timestamp range.
The rpc.discover request from a JSON-RPC client must be a valid JSON-RPC 2.0 request. The discovery method must not leak sensitive internal server information beyond the API schema.
All incoming RPC method calls must pass through namespace validation. Methods with the reserved 'rpc.' prefix must be identified as system methods and handled by the system namespace handler.
The OpenRPC document returned by rpc.discover must accurately reflect the current set of available methods and their parameter schemas at the time of the request.
If OpenRPC document generation fails, the server must return a well-defined JSON-RPC error response rather than an empty or malformed document.
The OpenRPC document must reflect only methods actually available at runtime, not theoretical or unimplemented methods.
Method signature conflicts in the OpenRPC document must be resolved deterministically; no two methods may share the same name with incompatible signatures.
RPC connections must use secure transport (HTTPS or IPC) to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks on discovery responses.
The 'rpc.' namespace prefix must be permanently reserved for system-defined methods. User-defined methods must never use this prefix.

The MODEXP precompile input must be parsed to extract base_length, exp_length, and mod_length as the first three 32-byte big-endian integers. Short inputs must be zero-padded, excess inputs must be ignored.

All operand bytes (base, exponent, modulus) must be extracted according to the parsed lengths. If input is shorter than required, missing bytes must be treated as zero. If input is longer, excess bytes must be ignored.
When modulus is zero, the MODEXP precompile must return a zero-valued byte array of length mod_length. Gas must still be charged for the computation.
The gas cost computed for MODEXP must accurately reflect the computational complexity using the multiplication complexity function and adjusted exponent length. Underestimation must not be possible.
Before executing modular exponentiation, available gas must be greater than or equal to the computed gas cost. If insufficient, execution must revert with out-of-gas error.
The MODEXP output must be exactly mod_length bytes, left-padded with zeros if the result is shorter. The result must equal (base^exp) mod modulus.
The MODEXP precompile must use arbitrary precision integer arithmetic. No integer overflow or truncation may occur during computation regardless of operand sizes.
When all three length fields (base_length, exp_length, mod_length) are zero, the precompile must return empty bytes and charge minimal gas. The behavior must be deterministic.
The 'highest bit' of the exponent used for adjusted exponent length computation must be defined as the position of the most significant set bit (0-indexed). For a zero exponent, this must yield 0.

The multiplication complexity function must be piecewise: for max_length <= 64, complexity = max_length^2; for 64 < max_length <= 1024, complexity = max_length^2/4 + 96*max_length - 3072; for max_length > 1024, complexity = max_length^2/16 + 480*max_length - 199680.

Provider.request() must validate RequestArguments structure before processing. Sensitive methods (eth_sendTransaction, personal_sign) must require explicit user authorization, returning error 4100 if unauthorized.
The wallet extension injecting the provider must do so in a way that page scripts cannot modify or intercept the provider object. Provider identity must be verifiable by DApps.
JSON-RPC responses from the Ethereum node must be validated for correct format. The connection must use secure transport. Request timeouts must be implemented to prevent indefinite hangs.

All provider errors must conform to the defined error codes: 4001 (user rejected), 4100 (unauthorized), 4200 (unsupported method), 4900 (disconnected), 4901 (chain disconnected). Each error must include code, message, and optional data fields.

Error code 4900 (disconnected) must indicate the provider is disconnected from all chains. Error code 4901 (chain disconnected) must indicate disconnection from a specific chain while the provider may still be connected to others.
The user must explicitly trust the injected provider. In multi-provider scenarios, the user must be able to select which provider to use.
Runtime isolation must exist between the DApp JavaScript context and the provider's internal state. The DApp must not be able to access provider private keys or internal signing mechanisms.

After Provider.request() completes successfully, the returned Promise must resolve with the JSON-RPC result field. On failure, it must reject with a ProviderRpcError containing the appropriate error code.
Request-to-JSON-RPC translation must not introduce injection vulnerabilities. Method names and parameters must be sanitized before constructing the JSON-RPC payload.
User approval UI must show clear, accurate information about what is being approved (transaction details, signing data). Phishing-resistant presentation is required.

Receipt responses from peer nodes must be validated: receipt count must match transaction count per block, individual receipt size must be bounded by gas_limit/8, and total response size must be bounded by the block gas limit.
GetReceipts request parameters from requesting peers must be validated. The firstBlockReceiptIndex must be within the valid range for the requested block. Response size must be bounded.
After receipt validation fails, the offending peer must be penalized (reputation decrease or disconnect). Buffer sizes must be bounded to prevent memory exhaustion.
The pagination protocol must guarantee eventual completeness: iterating with continuation indices must eventually yield all receipts for the requested blocks, assuming the peer is honest.
The message size limit for receipt responses must be consistently enforced across all peers. A concrete limit must be defined (not left ambiguous).
The gas/8 bound for individual receipt sizes must be derived from the block gas limit (~83M gas), ensuring no single receipt can exceed approximately 10MB.
After all three validation checks pass (receipt count, individual sizes, total size), the receipts buffer must be accepted for processing.
When the response fits within the message size limit, a complete response must be sent. When it does not fit, a partial response with continuation metadata must be sent.
The did_authenticate request must include a valid nonce for replay protection, a specified audience, and requested permission paths. The nonce must be verified for freshness before proceeding.
User consent must be obtained through a clear UI prompt before granting any DID authentication permissions. The prompt must display the requested paths and audience.
After successful authentication, the JWS token must be created with the correct DID, audience, nonce, and granted paths. The signature must be valid and verifiable.
When nonce verification fails, authentication must be refused with a defined error. The failure mode must not leak information about valid nonces.
After JWS creation, the token must contain a valid protected header with the signing algorithm, the DID key identifier, and the signed payload. The DID key must be correctly resolved.
Path matching for automatic JWE decryption must follow a well-defined semantic: only exact path matches or explicitly authorized wildcard patterns should allow auto-return without user prompt.
The wallet must use cryptographically secure implementations for JWS signing and JWE decryption. Private keys must never be exposed to the requesting DApp.
After JWE decryption, cleartext is returned only if paths match (auto-return) or user explicitly confirms. Unmatched paths without user confirmation must not return cleartext.
Light client bootstrap requests must be served with valid Merkle proofs for the sync committee. The light client must verify these proofs before trusting any bootstrap data.
Before creating a bootstrap object, the finalized block must be validated for eligibility: the block must have a finalized checkpoint and the sync committee must be available in the state.
After bootstrap construction, the bootstrap object must contain the light client header, the current sync committee, and a valid Merkle branch proving the sync committee against the state root.
Light client updates must only be created when sync committee participation meets a minimum threshold. The threshold must be explicitly defined.
Light client updates must be ranked using the is_better_update comparison function. The update with the highest quality (most participation, finality proof) must be preferred.
After creating light client updates, both finality updates and optimistic updates must be distributed to requesting light clients. Optimistic updates must be available even without finality proofs.
At least one honest full node must be available to serve correct light client data. Data withholding attacks cannot be detected cryptographically, so availability depends on network assumptions.

BN128 ADD precompile inputs must be validated: both input points must have coordinates less than the field modulus p, and each point must satisfy the curve equation y^2 = x^3 + 3 (mod p). Invalid points must cause OutOfGasError.
BN128 MUL precompile input must validate the G1 point on the curve. The scalar is an arbitrary 256-bit value requiring no validation. Gas cost of 6000 must accurately reflect worst-case computation.

BN128 Pairing precompile input length must be divisible by 192 bytes. All G1 points must be validated on the curve. All G2 points must be validated on the curve AND in the correct prime-order subgroup. Gas cost must be linear in the number of pairs.
All BN128 precompile failures (invalid input, insufficient gas) must uniformly raise OutOfGasError. No distinction between error types must be observable by the caller.
When BN128 precompile input is shorter than expected (less than 64 bytes for ADD, less than 96 bytes for MUL), missing bytes must be treated as zero-padded.
The subgroup order check for G2 points in the pairing precompile must verify that the point has order r (the prime order of the BN128 curve groups). Failure to check enables invalid pairing results.

The BN128 curve arithmetic library must correctly implement point addition, scalar multiplication, and optimal Ate pairing over the BN128 curve. Implementation errors would compromise all ZK proof verification on Ethereum.

The security of BN128 precompiles relies on the hardness of the Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm Problem (ECDLP) on the BN128 curve. The chosen curve parameters must provide adequate security margin.
Gas pricing for BN128 precompiles must accurately reflect computation cost: ADD=150, MUL=6000, Pairing=34000*k+45000 (where k is the number of pairs). Underpricing enables DoS attacks.
After BN128 ADD completes successfully, the output must be the 64-byte encoding of the sum of the two input G1 points on the BN128 curve.
After BN128 MUL completes successfully, the output must be the 64-byte encoding of the scalar multiple of the input G1 point.
After BN128 Pairing completes successfully, the output must be a single 32-byte value: 1 if the pairing check passes (product of pairings equals identity), 0 otherwise.
